name: Beef Bulgogi
blurb: Thin beef marinated in soy, pear and sesame, seared fast and served over rice with kimchi.
ingredients: 600g sirloin or rump steak, sliced as thinly as you can (freeze for 30 min first)
Steamed rice and kimchi, to serve
method: Mix the grated pear, soy, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and gochugaru in a bowl. Add the beef and turn to coat. Leave 20 minutes at room temperature (or up to a day in the fridge).
Get a large frying pan or wok very hot with a little neutral oil.
Lift the beef from the marinade, letting excess drip off, and sear in two batches for 2 minutes each so it browns rather than stews. Return all the beef to the pan.
Add the marinade and the spring onions and toss for 1 minute until the sauce is sticky and glossy.
Scatter with sesame seeds and serve over rice with kimchi.

name: Japchae (Korean Glass Noodles)
blurb: Sweet-potato glass noodles tossed with sesame, soy and a rainbow of quick-fried vegetables.
ingredients: 2 tbsp toasted sesame oil, plus extra
method: Boil the noodles for 6 minutes until slippery and just tender, drain, rinse under cold water and snip a few times with scissors. Toss with 1 tbsp each soy and sesame oil.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, refresh, squeeze dry and season with a little sesame oil and salt.
Fry each vegetable separately in a hot pan with a drop of oil, seasoning lightly, so each keeps its colour: onion and pepper 2 minutes, carrot 1 minute, mushrooms 3 minutes with the garlic.
Combine remaining soy, sugar and sesame oil in a large bowl. Add the noodles, spinach and all the vegetables and toss thoroughly with your hands so everything is glossed.
Warm through in the pan for a minute, then finish with sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
blurb: Chewy rice cakes simmered in a fiery, slightly sweet gochujang sauce with fish cake and spring onion.
ingredients: 500g fresh or vacuum-packed Korean rice cakes (tteok)
150g Korean fish cakes or firm tofu, sliced
method: If your rice cakes are firm or from the fridge, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes so they soften.
Whisk the gochujang, gochugaru, soy, sugar and garlic into the water in a wide pan and bring to a simmer.
Add the rice cakes and fish cakes and cook, stirring often so nothing sticks, for 8-10 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings and the rice cakes are chewy.
Stir in the spring onions and cook 1 minute more. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens too much.
Top with halved boiled eggs and sesame seeds and eat hot.

name: Korean Fried Chicken
blurb: Double-fried for shatter-crisp skin, then tossed in a sticky sweet-spicy gochujang glaze.
ingredients: 1kg chicken wings or boneless thighs, cut into 4cm pieces
1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp white pepper, 1 tbsp grated ginger
2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar
3 garlic cloves crushed, 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
method: Toss the chicken with the salt, pepper and ginger. Whisk the cornflour, flour and baking powder, then whisk in the sparkling water to a thin batter.
Heat 6cm of oil to 160C. Dip the chicken in batter, let the excess run off and fry in batches for 6 minutes. Lift out and rest on a rack.
Turn the heat up to 190C and fry each batch a second time for 3-4 minutes until deep gold and very crisp. Drain.
Warm the gochujang, honey, soy, vinegar and garlic in a wide pan until glossy and just bubbling.
Off the heat, add the chicken and toss to coat every piece. Finish with sesame seeds and serve at once.

name: Doenjang Jjigae
blurb: A quick, deeply savoury Korean soybean-paste stew with tofu, courgette and mushrooms.
method: Whisk the doenjang and gochugaru into the water in a pot and bring to a simmer.
Add the potato and onion and cook for 8 minutes until the potato is nearly tender.
Add the courgette, mushrooms and garlic and simmer 5 minutes.
Slip in the tofu and warm through for 3-4 minutes without stirring too hard so it stays whole.
Scatter with spring onions and serve bubbling hot with a bowl of rice on the side.

name: Jjajangmyeon (Korean Black Bean Noodles)
blurb: Chewy noodles under a glossy, savoury-sweet black bean sauce loaded with pork and diced vegetables.
ingredients: 300g pork shoulder or belly, cut into 1cm dice
method: Fry the chunjang gently in the oil for 3-4 minutes to take off its raw edge, then scrape into a bowl.
In the same pan, brown the pork over high heat. Add the onion, potato and courgette and fry for 6-8 minutes until softening.
Return the fried paste with the sugar and garlic, add 300ml water and simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook 1 minute to a glossy, thick sauce.
Cook the noodles, drain and divide between bowls. Ladle over the sauce and top with cucumber.

name: Weeknight Shoyu Ramen
blurb: A soy-based chicken broth with springy noodles, jammy egg, greens and quick-glazed chicken.
ingredients: 1 thumb ginger sliced, 4 garlic cloves smashed
4 nests ramen or medium egg noodles
4 spring onions sliced, 1 sheet nori, chilli oil to serve
method: Bring the stock, 2 tbsp soy, ginger, garlic and dried shiitake to a gentle simmer while you cook everything else. Strain before serving.
Boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes, cool in iced water and peel.

Sear the chicken thighs skin-side down in a dry pan for 6 minutes until golden, flip and cook 4 minutes more. Add the remaining soy, the mirin and sugar and bubble to a sticky glaze. Rest, then slice.
Cook the noodles to packet time; blanch the pak choi in the same water for the last minute.
Divide noodles between deep bowls, pour over the hot broth, and top with sliced chicken, a halved egg, pak choi, spring onions, torn nori and chilli oil.

name: Pan-Fried Pork Gyoza
blurb: Juicy pork and cabbage dumplings, crisped on one side and steamed on the other, with a sharp dipping sauce.
ingredients: 200g white cabbage, very finely chopped and salted for 10 min, then squeezed
2 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, grated
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
For dipping: 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp chilli oil
method: Mix the pork, squeezed cabbage, spring onions, garlic, ginger, soy, sesame oil and sugar until sticky.
Put a heaped teaspoon on each wrapper, wet the edge, fold into a half-moon and pleat one side to seal. Sit each on its base.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large lidded frying pan. Add a batch of gyoza flat-side down and fry for 2 minutes until golden underneath.
Pour in 80ml water, cover immediately and steam for 4-5 minutes until the water has gone and the wrappers are translucent. Uncover and fry 1 minute more to re-crisp the base.
Serve crisp-side up with the dipping sauce.

name: Okonomiyaki
blurb: A thick Osaka-style cabbage pancake topped with sauce, mayo, bonito and a snow of seaweed.
ingredients: 8 rashers streaky bacon or thin pork belly slices
For topping: okonomiyaki or brown sauce, Kewpie or regular mayo
Bonito flakes and aonori (seaweed flakes), to finish
method: Whisk the flour, dashi and eggs to a smooth batter. Fold in the cabbage and spring onions — it will look mostly cabbage, that's right.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium. Spoon in half the mixture and pat into a 2cm-thick round.
Lay half the bacon over the top, cook 5 minutes until set underneath, then flip carefully and cook 5 minutes more so the bacon crisps.
Flip once more, bacon-side up. Slide onto a plate.
Zigzag with sauce and mayo, then shower with bonito flakes and aonori. Repeat for the second pancake.

name: Chicken Karaage
blurb: Ginger-and-soy marinated chicken thighs in a light potato-starch crust, fried shatteringly crisp.
ingredients: 700g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 4cm pieces
Lemon wedges, Kewpie mayo and steamed rice, to serve
method: Mix the soy, sake, ginger, garlic, sugar and pepper. Add the chicken and marinate for 20 minutes.
Beat in the egg, then add the potato starch and toss so each piece wears a loose, craggy coating.
Heat 4cm of oil to 170C. Fry the chicken in batches for 4 minutes, lift out and rest for 3 minutes.
Return each batch to the oil for a second 1-2 minute fry at 185C until deep gold and crisp. Drain on a rack.
Serve hot with lemon wedges to squeeze over, a blob of mayo and plenty of rice.

name: Nikujaga
blurb: Japanese comfort food: thin beef and potatoes simmered in a sweet soy-dashi broth until meltingly soft.
ingredients: 300g thinly sliced beef (sukiyaki cut) or rump, sliced thin
100g mangetout or green beans, to finish
method: Sear the beef in a little oil in a wide pan just until it changes colour, then push to one side.
Add the onions and carrots and fry for 3 minutes, then add the potatoes.
Pour in the dashi, soy, mirin, sake and sugar. Bring to a simmer and lay a round of baking paper directly on the surface as a lid.
Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are very tender and the liquid has reduced by half.
Add the mangetout for the last 3 minutes. Let it sit off the heat for 10 minutes before serving — it tastes better warm than piping hot.

name: Lemongrass Pork Banh Mi
blurb: Griddled lemongrass pork in a crisp baguette with quick pickles, cucumber, chilli and herbs.
ingredients: 600g pork loin or shoulder steaks, thinly sliced
3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar
1 carrot and 1/2 daikon (or extra carrot), shredded
3 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, pinch salt (for the pickle)
4 short baguettes or 1 large, cut into 4
1/2 cucumber sliced, 1 red chilli sliced, coriander and mint sprigs
method: Mix the lemongrass, fish sauce, sugar, garlic and oil, add the pork and leave 20 minutes.
Toss the shredded carrot and daikon with the vinegar, sugar and salt and set aside to pickle.
Get a griddle or frying pan smoking hot and cook the pork in a single layer for 2 minutes each side until caramelised at the edges.
Split the baguettes, pull out a little crumb, and spread with mayo (and pate if using).
Fill with pork, drained pickle, cucumber, chilli and a good handful of herbs. Press shut and eat.

name: Caramel Black Pepper Pork
blurb: Vietnamese-style pork simmered in a dark palm-sugar caramel sharp with fish sauce and lots of pepper.
ingredients: 4 tbsp palm sugar or light brown sugar
3 spring onions and 1 red chilli, sliced, to finish
method: Melt the sugar in a dry heavy pan over medium heat until it turns a deep amber caramel — watch it closely.
Carefully add 2 tbsp water (it will spit), then the fish sauce, soy and black pepper.
Add the pork, shallots, garlic and ginger and turn to coat in the caramel.
Pour in the coconut water, bring to a simmer, half-cover and cook gently for 35-40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is tender and the sauce is syrupy and clings.
Scatter with spring onions and chilli and serve with rice.

name: Mee Goreng
blurb: Bold Malaysian fried noodles with chicken, egg and greens in a sweet, spicy, savoury sauce.
ingredients: 400g fresh yellow egg noodles (or 250g dried, cooked)
2 tbsp sambal oelek or chilli paste
150g choi sum or pak choi, chopped
100g beansprouts, fried shallots and lime, to serve
method: Mix the kecap manis, soy, sambal and ketchup in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 3 minutes until nearly cooked. Push aside, pour in the egg and scramble.
Add the garlic, tomato and greens and toss for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss constantly for 2 minutes until everything is coated and slightly caramelised at the edges.
Stir through the beansprouts, then serve topped with fried shallots and lime wedges.

name: Chicken Khao Soi
blurb: Northern Thai curry noodle soup: coconut broth over soft noodles, crowned with a tangle of crisp ones.
ingredients: 6 chicken thighs, bone-in if you can
3 tbsp khao soi or massaman curry paste, plus 1 tsp curry powder and 1 tsp turmeric
Oil, for frying a handful of the noodles until crisp
To serve: lime wedges, sliced shallots, pickled mustard greens, coriander, chilli oil
method: Fry the curry paste, curry powder and turmeric in 2 tbsp oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the thick cream from the top of one tin of coconut milk and cook until the oil splits, then add the chicken and turn to coat.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the stock, add fish sauce and sugar, and simmer gently for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Meanwhile, fry a small handful of raw noodles in hot oil until puffed and golden; drain. Boil the rest of the noodles and divide between deep bowls.
Ladle the curry and chicken over the noodles, top with the crisp noodles and serve the garnishes alongside for everyone to add.
